analogies.summary: This asymmetric hydrogenation process synthesizes tetrahydroquinoxalines and dihydroquinoxalinones using a rhodium-catalyzed outer-sphere mechanism in dichloromethane (DCM) solvent. The flow process operates in a microflow reactor with a 25-minute residence time at 0.083 mL/min flow rate under 20 bar back pressure, achieving 90% yield. The batch baseline required 18 hours at 25°C with 0.05 M concentration to achieve 99% yield in the same DCM solvent. Flow processing dramatically reduced reaction time from 18 hours to 25 minutes (43-fold acceleration) while maintaining high yield, though with a slight decrease from 99% to 90%. The significant time reduction represents the primary advantage of the continuous flow approach over traditional batch processing for this enantioselective transformation.
